record.title: Approval impact table leaves out unrecognized destructive segments and drops its documented 'could not compute' warning whenever an rm/curl segment is present
record.description: SandboxManager.preview builds the 'system-computed impact' list (시스템이 계산한 영향) on the exec approval card. It models only two verbs, rm and curl. README.md:380 states the compensating control: for any other command it shows '자동 계산 못 함' (could not compute) and the raw command. The code adds that note only when the whole command produced no affected rows and no notes (sandbox.py:872). A compound command from the agent such as 'rm /workspace/harmless.txt; find /workspace/keep -delete' or 'rm /workspace/a.txt; mv /workspace/important.db /tmp/gone' therefore produces one row, 'delete harmless.txt', and notes=[]. The find -delete or mv segment gets no row and no warning. The default policy sends the whole command to require_approval under rule rm-curl-needs-approval, whose reason text mentions only rm/curl. Both renderers (templates/_approvals.html:12-16 and cli.py:204-212) show the partial list as '(1건)' with no warning, and decide() then runs the complete stored command (service.py:415). Run alone, the same mv or find -delete would have shown the could-not-compute warning. The agent cannot delete workspace files without approval (delete_file and non-allowlisted exec need approval). So a prompt-injected agent can get a deletion or rename it could not do on its own executed under the human's approval, while the system-computed impact summary marks the action as only the benign deletion. The raw command text is still shown verbatim above the table, so the approver can see the extra segment if they read it. The defect is that the documented 'could not compute' safety net silently fails for compound commands. Overwrite-only payloads (dd of=, '> file') add nothing beyond the agent's own authority, because write_file overwrites are allowed without approval in the default policy.
record.root_cause: SandboxManager.preview (agentbox/sandbox.py:814-874) adds affected rows only in the name == 'rm' (line 824) and name == 'curl' (line 846) branches. It has no else branch for other segments. Its only fallback note is gated on `if not affected and not notes` (line 872), so it covers the whole command, not each segment. One rm or curl row makes `affected` non-empty, and that suppresses the warning for every other unmodeled segment. The substitution heuristic at line 818 checks only '$', backtick, '<(' and 'eval '. This contradicts the documented behavior in README.md:380, which says commands other than rm/curl show '자동 계산 못 함' together with the raw command.
record.intended_behavior: When any segment of the stored exec command is not one the preview can model, the approval card must say that the computed impact is incomplete and that the raw command must be read, as README.md:380 promises. This must hold whether or not other segments produced rows. A partial impact list must never be shown as the complete system-computed impact with no warning.

trace.description: An agent token holder (lowest-trust network principal, own sandbox only, line 207) submits an exec tool call with a fully attacker-chosen command string.
Policy returns REQUIRE_APPROVAL (rule rm-curl-needs-approval for any command containing rm/curl), so _preview builds the impact stored with the approval and shown to the human.
For tool == 'exec', delegates to sandboxes.preview(sid, command) with the agent's raw command.
Iterates _split_segments(command). Only the rm (824) and curl (846) branches append rows. mv, find -delete, dd, redirection targets and every other segment are skipped with no row and no note.
The could-not-compute note is added only when `not affected and not notes`. The rm/curl row makes affected non-empty, so the warning for the unmodeled segment is suppressed.
Renders '시스템이 계산한 영향 (1건)' with only the rm row. The notes loop at line 16 shows no warning. cli.py:204-212 (_show_approval) prints the same partial list with no notes.
After the human approves, the complete stored args, including the unlisted mv / find -delete segment, run via _run_tool under the human's approval (after the AP-2 snapshot at line 406).

evidence.description: `if name == "rm":` and `elif name == "curl":` (line 846) are the only branches that add impact rows. There is no else branch for other verbs.
`if not affected and not notes:` gates the only '시스템이 영향 파일을 계산하지 못함. 명령 원문을 확인할 것.' note on the whole command.
The substitution warning checks only '$', '`', '<(' and 'eval '. Unrecognized verbs and redirection are not flagged.
Documents the compensating control: preview only knows rm and curl, and other commands show '자동 계산 못 함' plus the raw command. That promise does not hold for compound commands that include rm/curl.

rm-curl-needs-approval routes any command containing rm/curl to require_approval (verified locally for all compound payloads). write_file has no rule and is allowed under default: allow (line 10). delete_file (line 18) and non-allowlisted exec (line 30) require approval, so deletion and rename are not within the agent's direct authority.
Labels preview.affected as '시스템이 계산한 영향 (N건)'. Line 16 iterates preview.notes as the only warning channel. Line 8 shows the raw command in a <pre>.
The terminal approver prints the same '시스템이 계산한 영향' list (204-208) and notes (211-212), so it inherits the same omission.
decide() runs the full stored args after the pre-execution snapshot (line 406).

conditions.description: Attacker holds the agent token for its own sandbox (assumed prompt-injected per the threat model).
A human approver approves based on the system-computed impact table and its warnings, without spotting the extra segment in the raw command shown above the table.
Default policy is in force, which routes the compound command to require_approval rather than deny.
The compound command contains at least one rm or curl segment, so affected is non-empty. An rm operand that does not exist still yields a 'does not exist' row.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected agent sends one exec whose first segment is a benign rm (or curl) and whose later segment deletes or renames a file the agent cannot delete without approval. The approval card's system-computed impact then lists only the benign deletion and shows no could-not-compute warning.
payloads: rm /workspace/harmless.txt; dd if=/dev/zero of=/workspace/important.db bs=1M count=10
instructions: Inside the sbx5 sandbox (audited source read-only at /target, no network, no Docker), import agentbox.sandbox and call SandboxManager.preview as an unbound function on a dummy object. The dummy provides _container, plus _expand/_walk resolving against a fixed in-memory set of /workspace paths. Only these Docker-backed helpers are stubbed. The segment loop and the line 872 gate run unmodified.
Call preview for each compound payload and for the lone mv / find -delete / dd baselines, and record affected and notes.
Run agentbox.policy.Policy.load(default_policy.yaml).decide on the same commands, and on write_file and delete_file, to confirm routing and the agent's direct authority.
execution.observed_result: Every compound payload returned only the rm/curl row (for example affected=[{path: /workspace/harmless.txt, effect: 삭제}] or the curl 외부 접속 row) and notes=[]. The find -delete, mv and dd segments got no row and no warning. The lone baselines 'mv /workspace/important.db /tmp/gone', 'find /workspace/keep -delete' and 'dd ... of=/workspace/important.db' each returned affected=[] and notes=['시스템이 영향 파일을 계산하지 못함. 명령 원문을 확인할 것.']. Policy routed all compound commands to require_approval (rm-curl-needs-approval, matched [rm]), lone mv to exec-needs-approval and delete_file to delete-file-needs-approval. write_file overwrite was allow. Captured in agents/v17/artifacts/v17.out and agents/v17/artifacts/v17-policy.out. The approval UI was not rendered live and nothing was executed.

remediation.strategy: Make the preview fail closed per segment. For every _split_segments segment the preview does not model, including bare redirection-target segments, add a note naming that segment and telling the approver to read the raw command. Keep the global fallback for an empty result. Optionally flag '>'/'>>' redirection next to the substitution heuristic, and label the table as partial whenever any segment was unmodeled.

likelihood.reason: Building the compound command is trivial and fully under agent control, and the default policy routes it to approval. Success still depends on the approver trusting the impact table and warnings rather than reading the raw command. The raw command is shown verbatim directly above the table (web <pre>, CLI per-line with line count).

impact.reason: The gain beyond the agent's own authority is a deletion or rename of /workspace files (mv, find -delete, etc.) executed under the human's approval without being shown in the system-computed impact. Overwrites (dd, redirection) are already allowed to the agent via write_file, so they add nothing. Effects stay inside the network=none sandbox's /workspace, and decide() takes an unconditional AP-2 snapshot before execution (service.py:406), so files can be restored.

confidence.reason: Source shows the per-command gate. A bounded sandboxed harness ran the real preview() and policy code, stubbing only the Docker glob/walk helpers, and reproduced the suppressed warning against lone-command baselines. Live rendering in the card was not exercised, but both templates display preview.affected/notes verbatim per source.
